brief: Goldman's Jason Klein gives a quarter-end read on US equity market liquidity. Headline: YTD 2026 volumes average a record 19B shares and $1T executed value a day, up 10% y/y through Q3, yet top-of-book liquidity is flat and the trading environment stays fragile. Executed value has doubled since 2023 ($511B to $1,041B daily) while top-of-book size fell 21% over the same stretch. June had the two busiest volume days ever (33B shares 6/18, 32B shares 6/26), but top-of-book liquidity that month plunged 33% versus May before recovering to YTD highs. Since 2017, top-of-book depth is down 76% even as daily share volume nearly tripled, and depth has stabilized at $11M/day for the last two years. Conclusion: despite the shift to a structurally higher-volume regime, top-of-book depth still evaporates in stressed tapes, thinnest exactly when it is needed most.
